From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From sub- (“sub-, under”) +‎ marino (“marine; of the sea”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /submaˈɾino/ [s̺ub.maˈɾi.nʊ]
  • Rhymes: -ino
  • Hyphenation: sub‧ma‧ri‧no

Adjective

[edit]

submarino (feminine submarina, masculine plural submarinos, feminine plural submarinas)

  1. underwater; submarine

Noun

[edit]

submarino m (plural submarinos)

  1. submarine (undersea boat)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “submarino”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • “submarino”, in Dicionário Estraviz de galego (in Galician), 2014–2026

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
submarino
Wikipedia pt

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • submarinho (uncommon)

Etymology

[edit]

From sub- (“sub-, under”) +‎ marino (“marine; of the sea”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /su.bi.maˈɾĩ.nu/, /sub.maˈɾĩ.nu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /su.bi.maˈɾĩ.nu/, /sub.maˈɾĩ.nu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /sub.maˈɾi.no/, /su.bi.maˈɾi.no/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /su.bmɐˈɾi.nu/ [su.βmɐˈɾi.nu]

  • Hyphenation: sub‧ma‧ri‧no

Noun

[edit]

submarino m (plural submarinos)

  1. submarine; U-boat (undersea boat)

Adjective

[edit]

submarino (feminine submarina, masculine plural submarinos, feminine plural submarinas, not comparable)

  1. submarine; underwater
    Synonyms: imerso, subaquático, submarinho, submerso

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • epipelágico, mesopelágico, batipelágico, abissopelágico

Coordinate terms

[edit]
  • aéreo, superficial, terrestre

Related terms

[edit]
  • submarinho
  • submarinista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “submarino”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “submarino”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From sub- +‎ marino.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /submaˈɾino/ [suβ̞.maˈɾi.no]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ino
  • Syllabification: sub‧ma‧ri‧no

Adjective

[edit]

submarino (feminine submarina, masculine plural submarinos, feminine plural submarinas)

  1. submarine, undersea, subsea, underwater

Derived terms

[edit]
  • submarinismo

Noun

[edit]

submarino m (plural submarinos)

  1. submarine
  2. waterboarding

Derived terms

[edit]
  • antisubmarino
  • cazasubmarinos

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Tagalog: submarino

Further reading

[edit]
  • “submarino”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish submarino (“submarine”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /submaˈɾino/ [sʊb.mɐˈɾiː.n̪o]
  • Rhymes: -ino
  • Syllabification: sub‧ma‧ri‧no

Noun

[edit]

submarino (Baybayin spelling ᜐᜓᜊ᜔ᜋᜇᜒᜈᜓ)

  1. submarine (underswater vessel)
    • 2007, Kasiya-siyang Pagbasa N' 2007 Ed.‎[1], Rex Bookstore, Inc., →ISBN, page 117:
      Ang submarino ay isang sasakyang ginagamit sa ilalim ng dagat.
      A submarine is a vehicle that is used underwater.
